1.pericope_label: For Zion’s sake will I not hold my peace, and for Jerusalem’s sake I will not rest, until the righteousness thereof go forth as brightness, and the salvation thereof as a lamp that burneth. And the Gentiles shall see thy righteousness, and thou shalt be called by a new name, which the mouth of the Lord shall name. Thou shalt also be a crown of glory in the hand of the Lord. Thou shalt no more be termed Forsaken; but thou shalt be called Hephzibah, and thy land Beulah

schools.summary: Lays the three candidates for the speaker side by side and prefers the Servant as most in harmony with what follows, corrects the comparisons to the brightness of morning and a burning torch, reads the withholding of the new name as deliberate, since the promise is heightened by its absence as something meant to transcend all experience, distinguishes the kingly crown from the priestly tiara and the two words for hand, and anchors the two new names in the marriage of Hezekiah with a queen who bore the first of them.

Reports the rival identifications of the speaker, God himself and Israel in captivity, before settling on the prophet speaking out of love for the church; divides the righteousness between the innocence of her case and her justifying righteousness, keeps the crown in the hand for safety as much as for show, and refuses any allusion to sons marrying their mother as exceedingly disagreeable, preferring the older versions that read dwell with.

Gives the opening words to God declaring his purpose, or else keeps the prophet and adds the interval, since the man resolving here lived near two hundred years before the thing was done; supplies the new name outright, explains that in the prophets a desolate land appears as a widow and an inhabited land as a married woman, and attacks the text of the last verse, where the particles of comparison are missing though the versions seem to have read them.

Keeps the prophet as speaker and makes him a type of Christ, indefatigable in his office and instant in preaching and in prayer alike, since the business of ministers is to speak from God to his people and to God for his people, and in neither may they be silent.

debates.question: Who is it that will not hold his peace?

positions.view: the prophet, out of love for the church, against those who make it God himself or Israel in captivity
God, declaring his purpose about what the preceding chapter foretold
opinions differ between prophet, Servant and God; the Servant is most in harmony with what follows, carrying on what a later theology would call mediatorial intercession
the prophet, resolving to solicit God despite the interval of near two hundred years before fulfilment
the prophet, herein a type of Christ, continuing instant both in preaching and in prayer

debates.question: Is the new name given or withheld?

positions.view: given, and it is Christian, or else the name that follows in the fourth verse
given in the next verse, one name answering to her condition and another to her relation
withheld: the effect of the promise is heightened by the absence of the name, as something meant to transcend all experience
new names simply take the place of the old

debates.question: How can sons marry their mother?

positions.view: they cannot: the thing is exceedingly disagreeable and no allusion to it is possible, so the older versions read dwell with rather than marry, and the sense is that thy sons shall have thee

the text is at fault: the particles of comparison are missing from the Hebrew though the versions seem to have read them, and a scholar would read builder rather than sons, though little is gained by it
the figure is turned about, the people in their collective unity being the bridegroom and the country the bride, whom they are bound as a husband to cherish and protect
the words may stand as they are, the young man marrying the maiden and the children marrying the city

outliers.reading: Anchors the two new names in history, tracing the first to Hezekiah's marriage with a queen who bore it, which on the assumption of this prophet's authorship would have been fresh in his memory, and finding it after his manner to read an omen in a bride's name as in the names of his own sons; the confirmation, he adds, is that the word for Forsaken had itself been borne by an earlier queen. He also concludes that the crown is not worn but held out, God being crowned from eternity already, so that this new glory is displayed in the hand for the nations to gaze at.

Supplies the usage behind the second name, that in the prophets a desolate land appears under the figure of a widow and an inhabited land under that of a married woman who has both husband and children; and cites a traveller for the eastern custom by which the unmarried take virgins and widowers widows.

themes: For Zion’s sake will I not hold my peace, and for Jerusalem’s sake I will not rest, until the righteousness thereof go forth as brightness, and the salvation thereof as a lamp that burneth.
And the Gentiles shall see thy righteousness, and all kings thy glory: and thou shalt be called by a new name, which the mouth of the Lord shall name.
Thou shalt also be a crown of glory in the hand of the Lord, and a royal diadem in the hand of thy God.

Thou shalt no more be termed Forsaken; neither shall thy land any more be termed Desolate: but thou shalt be called Hephzi–bah, and thy land Beulah: for the Lord delighteth in thee, and thy land shall be married.
For as a young man marrieth a virgin, so shall thy sons marry thee: and as the bridegroom rejoiceth over the bride, so shall thy God rejoice over thee.

6.pericope_label: I have set watchmen upon thy walls, O Jerusalem, which shall never hold their peace day nor night: ye that make mention of the Lord, keep not silence, and give him no rest, till he establish, and till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth. The Lord hath sworn by his right hand, Surely I will no more give thy corn to be meat for thine enemies. Go through, go through the gates; prepare ye the way of the people. Say ye to the daughter of Zion, Behold, thy salvation cometh

schools.summary: Reduces the identifications of the watchmen to angelic guardians or prophets and prefers the second, instancing the prophets of the return and of the Christian church, corrects the people addressed beside them into the remembrancers whose office is to remind God of his promises, recognises in the oath the principle that God can swear by nothing less than what is identified with his own greatness, and argues from a plural that the Gentiles are thought of as escorting Israel home.

Eliminates angels, kings, magistrates and the mourners in Zion before settling the watchmen on ministers of the gospel, and draws out the figure of men set on a city wall who must keep their stand, descry an enemy and defend the outworks; rejects the view that the arm sworn by is Christ, on the ground that God is said to swear to him and about him but never by him, and takes the gates for those of the church in the latter day, open night and day to converts of either nation.

Alone reconstructs the practice behind the image, from a temple watch kept day and night by the Levites and probably by the singers among them, to eastern watches still kept by a loud cry that marks the hour and proves the watchman awake, and reads a short psalm as nothing but the alternating cry of two divisions of that watch; finds the law of the tithe behind the eating in the courts, and sets the four closing names in inverted order.

Presses the duty of the watchmen, since the church is a besieged city whose sentinels must be wakeful and willing to endure hardness, never off watch while those they watch for are in danger and never betraying the cause by a cowardly silence, adds that the people must not think it enough that their watchmen pray for them, and keeps the historical picture of gates thrown open and a road cast up for the return.

debates.question: Who are the watchmen on the walls?

positions.view: ministers of the gospel, not angels, kings, magistrates or the mourners in Zion; the figure asks courage, constancy, vigilance and sobriety together
prophets rather than angelic guardians, though two passages may be pleaded for the latter; the prophets of the return and of the Christian church are the representative examples
ministers, sentinels of a besieged city, never off watch while those they watch for are in danger
the faithful, and in particular the priests and Levites, the image being drawn from the temple watch
not by Christ, since God is said to swear to him and about him but never by him, so omnipotence is meant, and the force is that he stakes his being the omnipotent God he is on the performance
by nothing less than what is identified with his own greatness, on the principle of a later epistle; the promise exactly reverses the curse of the law
the result is that the church will no longer succumb to worldly power

debates.question: Whose gates are to be gone through?

positions.view: the gates of the church in the latter day, open night and day so that converts of either nation may enter
the gates of Babylon, thrown open for a return along a road cast up and cleared of stones, with standards set up so the people may embody for safety
the cry is the prophet's to heralds who summon the exiles, and the plural, peoples rather than people, shows the Gentiles escorting Israel, which makes the command addressed to the returning exiles

outliers.reading: Alone reconstructs the practice behind the image of the sleepless watchmen, taking it from the temple service where a constant watch was kept day and night by the Levites and this part seemingly fell to the singers, noting that eastern watches are still kept by a loud cry raised from time to time both to mark the hour and to prove the watchman awake, which explains why watchmen are elsewhere told to lift up the voice and why the bitterest reproach against them is that they are dumb dogs, and reading a short psalm as nothing but the alternating cry of two divisions of that watch.
Keeps both senses of the word rendered remembrancers, men who put God in mind of his promise and men who make the Lord to be remembered by putting his people in mind of him.

themes: I have set watchmen upon thy walls, O Jerusalem, which shall never hold their peace day nor night: ye that make mention of the Lord, keep not silence,
And give him no rest, till he establish, and till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth.

The Lord hath sworn by his right hand, and by the arm of his strength, Surely I will no more give thy corn to be meat for thine enemies; and the sons of the stranger shall not drink thy wine, for the which thou hast laboured:
But they that have gathered it shall eat it, and praise the Lord; and they that have brought it together shall drink it in the courts of my holiness.
Go through, go through the gates; prepare ye the way of the people; cast up, cast up the highway; gather out the stones; lift up a standard for the people.
Behold, the Lord hath proclaimed unto the end of the world, Say ye to the daughter of Zion, Behold, thy salvation cometh; behold, his reward is with him, and his work before him.
And they shall call them, The holy people, The redeemed of the Lord: and thou shalt be called, Sought out, A city not forsaken.
